independent_visual_counts.basis: Fresh native original full-page views, one page at a time, followed by bounded original pixel crops. Formula numerators and denominators sharing one printed equation count once; real wrapped text/formulas count each physical row. Footer decorations plus page number count once.

causal_chain: Both raw fragments are shorter than 0.2*glyph_h=12.6 and wider than 2*glyph_h=126, but they exempt each other from isolation: boundary distance 3428-3414=14 is below 1.5*glyph_h=94.5.
Their actual components are very small and scattered, so they do not meet the dense joined shallow blemish predicate, whose minimum component height is 0.35*glyph_h=22.05.
The first merge joins the two fragments because distance 14 is below merge_gap=25.2. This creates a 30-pixel aggregate band although no noise component is taller than 10 pixels.
The final filter requires aggregate band_h<0.4*typical_h=26.8. The merged height is 30, so thin=false, short-glyph inspection is skipped, decoration=false, and the false row remains.

component_evidence.id_warning: Original IDs 901/906 differ from production counting-mask IDs 891/896 because the production mask removes edge pixels. Coordinate boxes and areas agree; IDs are mask-local.

footer_control.warning: The projection band ends at 3207 whereas a real digit component ends at 3209. Preserve the source pixels and the one footer row, not a guessed bbox trim.

minimal_general_fix_proposal.preferred_location: The neighbor-evidence predicate in the isolated thin streak filter, layout.py:200.
minimal_general_fix_proposal.change: Do not allow another shallow broad fragment lacking glyph or coherent rule support to count as the neighboring numerator/glyph row that makes a candidate non-isolated. Classify supporting neighbors from a frozen counting-mask view so two or more shallow noise fragments cannot support each other by proximity alone.
minimal_general_fix_proposal.component_support: Use the existing page-derived glyph scale and connected-component boxes. A compact real glyph or a substantive numerator/denominator row may provide support; a broad union of sub-glyph specks with no connected fraction-rule topology does not. For this source the 73 noise components have max height 10, below the already-existing 0.2*glyph_h=12.6 candidate threshold, and the real footer is 197 pixels away.
minimal_general_fix_proposal.predicted_local_effect: Both unsupported streak fragments become isolated rather than mutual exceptions, so no spurious merged 30-pixel text row is created. This remains a prediction pending the parent's implementation and actual-page verification.
retain: Existing compact single-digit quotient recovery and real footer glyphs.
Fraction rules with real neighboring numerator/denominator glyphs.
Counting-only ink copy; extraction and all original PNG pixels unchanged.
reject: Ignoring everything below a footer or at a book-specific coordinate.
Only raising the final thin-band threshold: 30 pixels is an aggregate noise-union height, not evidence of a real glyph.
Filtering solely by total band width or height, which are inflated by distant specks.

causal_chain: The numerator of the right fraction contains two inner fractions, extending the upper projection band to 136 pixels.

The outer fraction rules and their denominator glyphs share a lower 67-pixel projection band. There is no thin raw projection band representing the outer rules, although those rules are plainly present as connected components.

The first merge's separate_full_text guard looks only for a thin raw projection band. It therefore marks the numerator and rule/denominator band as two complete text rows and blocks a merge despite the 6-pixel boundary distance.
The existing _single_fraction_row helper returns true on the complete 1362..1569 region at glyph scale 63, but this first-merge guard does not consult fraction topology.

Second-stage spill recovery cannot help: minimum height 67 is not below 0.75*line_h=49.5, the noisy projections are not aligned, and the width ratio does not meet fraction_spill. The two erroneous bands reach the final output unchanged.

component_topology.relationship: Both outer bars are on the same physical equation baseline to within 1 pixel. Numerator glyphs sit above the proposed split; denominator glyphs sit below their outer bar in the corresponding bar's x interval. The outer bars are inside the lower retained band, not literally crossing the five empty split rows.

false_positives.present_protection: 78 exceeds merge_gap 25.2; the actual lower ac. row must remain separate.

existing_helper_limit.why_not_a_universal_exemption: The helper can treat ordinary short glyph strokes as rules, erase whole rule-associated columns, and use a relative 25%-of-maximum residual-row threshold that loses a shorter second row. It is supporting evidence, not a proof of one row.
existing_helper_limit.not_a_third_requested_defect: These false positives document the risk of a proposed repair. Current gap guards still preserve the two source cases; no separate tool change is authorized here.

minimal_general_fix_proposal.preferred_location: The missing-rule clause of separate_full_text, layout.py:311.
minimal_general_fix_proposal.change: Allow component-supported outer-fraction topology to defeat the complete-text guard even when a rule is bundled with denominator glyphs in a non-thin projection band. Retain the existing short-gap, tall-row, and different_stacked_rows guards.
topology_requirements: Find a connected long shallow outer fraction bar at or near the candidate split, using existing glyph-relative scale rather than book coordinates. This source has widths 300/401, both above 2*glyph_h=126, and heights 10/8, below 0.2*glyph_h=12.6.

Require numerator components from the upper candidate and denominator components from the lower candidate in that same bar interval, with the denominator below the bar. A bare minus sign or an unrelated horizontal text stroke is not enough.
Reject a merge if supported glyphs reveal a separate second prose/equation row outside the fraction structure. Do not suppress a short lower row only because its ink density is lower.
Use the existing _single_fraction_row only as an additional consistency check, not as an unrestricted replacement for the full-text guard.
minimal_general_fix_proposal.predicted_local_effect: The two bands of the 1362..1569 nested-numerator equation become one printed row; subsequent tall-band expansion already has fraction recognition. The parent's actual implementation must confirm this rather than assuming a new 18-row pass.
retain: Stacked operands/results and brace-connected multiple-equation row safeguards.
Real wrapped prose and ac. formula continuation rows.
All formula pixels, formula content, and transcription line breaks.
reject: Ignoring the lower band or adding a fake Markdown line.
A special-case formula string, page coordinate, or book ID.

actual_source_cases.purpose: Full fragmented speck union must not acquire a glyph from its aggregate dimensions.
Small page digit and decorations survive.
A short real final text row survives.
Two ordinary text/formula rows stay separate.
True text rows only 16 pixels apart stay separate despite equations, minus signs, and punctuation.
The defective nested numerator is one equation.
Unrelated right-side specks must not replace fraction topology with noisy alignment.
An ordinary fraction with inline prose and formula label remains one row.
Known helper false positive; retain the short second prose row.
A fraction-filled row followed by genuine ac. continuation is two rows.
Nested numerator and denominator remain one printed equation.

case_evidence_convention.warning: These are bounded pixel evidence with independent expectations, not implemented-repair test results. Whole-page counts must include both real footers.

proposed_future_general_cases.basis: Source p8 establishes non-text fragmented noise. Future fixtures should vary pair/group size and separation so shallow fragments can form a tall bounding union without a glyph.
Production explicitly preserves single quotient digits such as 1 and 7. Retain this behavior even below the ordinary row projection threshold.
A thin rule supported by actual fraction glyphs is not an isolated scan streak; vary nested numerator/denominator sizes independently.
Two actual equation rows remain two even with minus signs, long horizontal glyph strokes, similar widths, or a short lower row.
The source-transcription contract counts each actual printed equation row, not a whole brace-connected object once.
Production preserves stacked operand/result row identities; an arithmetic rule must not be mistaken for a fraction bar.
